title: Valid Parentheses
statement:
Given a string `s` containing only the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, determine whether the input is valid.

The string is valid when every bracket is closed by the **same type** of bracket, brackets close in the **correct order**, and every closing bracket has a matching opener.

An empty string is valid.

steps.caption: Read left to right, remembering every opener.
'(' opens, so remember it — it is now the one that must be closed next.
'{' opens, so remember it — it is now the one that must be closed next.
'[' opens, so remember it — it is now the one that must be closed next.
']' matches the '[' on top, so that pair is settled and comes off.
'}' matches the '{' on top, so that pair is settled and comes off.
')' matches the '(' on top, so that pair is settled and comes off.
Every character read and nothing left open — balanced.
New string: "([)]" — the counts match, so only order can betray it.
'(' opens, so remember it — it is now the one that must be closed next.
'[' opens, so remember it — it is now the one that must be closed next.
')' needs '(' on top, but the top is '['. The most recent opener is the only one it may close.

checkpoints.question: Three openers are being held and the next character is ']'. Which one is it allowed to close?
options: the first opener, '(', since it opened the whole string
any '[' still being held, wherever it is
checkpoints.why: Brackets nest, so a closer always answers the innermost thing still open. That is exactly what 'most recent' means, and it is why a stack fits.

checkpoints.question: This string has two openers and two closers, and the next character is ')'. Is it still valid?
options: no — the top is '[', so ')' arrives out of order
yes — the counts match, so every bracket has a partner
not yet decidable — the last character decides it
checkpoints.answer: no — the top is '[', so ')' arrives out of order
checkpoints.why: Counting is blind to order. '[' opened after '(' and is still unclosed, so nothing but ']' may come next. This is the case that separates counting from a stack.

hints: Counting brackets is not enough. What makes the string on the right wrong when both have two openers and two closers?
When a closing bracket arrives, only one opener is allowed to answer it: the most recent one that is still unclosed. Everything older has to wait its turn.

Read left to right. Remember each opener in the order you meet them, and when a closer arrives, check it against the most recently remembered opener — if it matches, that pair is settled and both are forgotten. The string is valid when nothing is left waiting at the end.
